pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: crates/table-app/src/pipeline/shield_gate.rs:113 The only production call into the scam shield hard-codes this input, so the BLOCK rule for friends-and-family payment can never fire outside table-shield's unit tests, and a deal asking for it is judged as if it had not.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-app/src/pipeline/shield_gate.rs:113 The caller supplies the value that satisfies the rule; a search of crates found no other production writer of ShieldRule::FriendsAndFamily. The unit test at crates/table-shield/src/lib.rs:195 proves the rule only with an input production never passes. The payee rule's matching self-comparison on line 112 is covered separately by raise_payee_mismatch in send.rs.

crates/table-app/src/checks.rs:533 On a rescue deal shield_gate.rs:99-104 runs no rules and defaults to Clear, yet compose_rescue keeps this line, so the owner reads 'looks safe' and 'rules re-run now' over a skip that is never announced. The fail-closed branches for an unreadable shield or mandate do hold.

crates/table-app/src/pipeline/shield_gate.rs:151 A release counts only if it names the rule of every holding input; BLOCK cannot be released, and an unnamed rule is never covered (table-core shield.rs:43).
crates/table-app/src/checks/pipeline_facts.rs:106 The checklist line comes from the same mandate check the money steps run, not a second evaluator.
crates/table-app/src/pipeline/shield_gate.rs:188 A disallowed verdict falls through to a recorded refusal and Err(Error::Permission) before any money operation.
crates/table-app/src/checks.rs:561 Could-not-run is its own failing line with distinct words, never folded into a pass.

crates/table-app/src/checks.rs:546 The one remedy named is reachable in the approval window through shield_release. Most other Fail lines name no remedy, which this technique leaves to its neighbours.
crates/table-app/src/pipeline/send.rs:243 The payee check reads PayPal's record, not anything the counterparty being judged wrote.
